This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on secrets management so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer explicit, readable secrets management solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
2. Measure before optimizing any secrets management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Keep secrets management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Keep secrets management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Before starting secrets management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. When secrets management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
7. Validate secrets management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new secrets management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of secrets management correctness.
- Do not silently drop secrets management edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting secrets management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic secrets management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about secrets management over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
